subject: 🏃 Sunday — Presidio Half Marathon: The Pivot Test (Wk 7)
html:
Tomorrow you race the Presidio Half Marathon — the pivot test that decides whether SF stays 3:30 or upgrades to 3:25. The taper is done. Knee 1/5 all week, threshold reps dead-even at 7:09–7:13/mi on Tuesday, strides clean Friday. You're as ready as the plan could make you in 7 weeks.

Race-morning fuel (3+ hrs pre-gun): Oatmeal + banana (~50–60 g carbs), 16 oz water with the other half of an LMNT packet. Nothing new. Sip water until ~30 min out, then stop — you don't want a sloshing stomach on the bridge climb.

Gear check before you leave: H10 strap (confirm "Polar H10 — Connected" on the watch before the corral), bib, handheld with ½–¾ LMNT packet mixed at normal strength, 3 PF30 gels (carry all 3, plan to take 2 — the 3rd is a caffeine PF30 insurance policy). Take gel #1 at T−5 minutes in the corral.

Execution — effort-shaped, HR-governed:

  • Miles 1–2 (flat start): 7:15 / 7:10. Resist the adrenaline. This is where races get ruined — settle into rhythm, don't bank time. Let the crowd go.
  • Miles 3–4 (Climb 1 to the peak): 7:45 / 8:20. Run the effort, give the pace back. The 8:20 is correct — don't fight the hill.
  • Miles 5–6 (bridge + descent): 7:25 / 7:00. Controlled on the descent — shorten stride, quick cadence, don't bomb it (patellofemoral's least-favorite stimulus).
  • Mile 6.5 dip: Take gel #2 before Climb 2 begins. Chase with water from an aid station.
  • Miles 7–8 (Climb 2): 7:40 / 8:20. Same discipline — effort even, let pace float.
  • Mile 9 checkpoint (crest of Climb 2): Target ≤1:08:15 elapsed. If you're there, the math works — the descent and flat finish bank the rest.
  • Miles 9–10 (descent): 7:20 / 7:00. Optional caffeine PF30 (#3) at mi 9–10, before the build — take it if appetite allows, skip if it balks.
  • Mile 10 decision point: Check in — HR controlled? Knee silent? If both green, you have permission to press.
  • Miles 11–13 (the press + kick): 7:00 / 7:05 / 6:55, then kick the last 200m. Final-3 HR gate is live from ~mi 10.1 — avg must stay <170. The descent banks HR margin so you can build on the flat without dragging the average over. Hold the true kick to the last ~200m — a single end-spike won't move the 3-mi average and doubles as an opportunistic near-max-HR capture.

The three gates (all required to upgrade): (1) Sub-1:37:30 finish — the pacing above delivers ~1:36:54 with a ~36s cushion. (2) Avg HR <170 in the final 3 miles. If HR climbs past ~169, hold — don't push. (3) Zero knee compensation crossing the line. The knee outranks everything.

Focus cue: patience on the climbs, discipline on the descents. The two 8:20 miles are features of the course, not failures of the race. Make the time back on the bridge and the flat finish — don't chase it uphill. And on every descent: short stride, quick cadence, protect the knee. A clean 1:38 beats a 1:36 that fails the compensation gate.

Where you are: Week 7 of 12, end of Phase 2. This is the one race in the plan designed to answer a question. The data says you're ready — now go find out. Trust the HR, trust the taper, and race your race. Good luck tomorrow.
